analysis.lean: No bet on the side or total: the model and market agree, so Boston is a clear favorite to win but the -12.5 spread is priced fairly.
why: Our blended projection is Boston by 12.4 with a total of 222.4, against the market's -12.5 and 222.5. The market fair prices are 0.501 to cover and 0.502 over, so there is no edge either way.
The ratings favor Boston: net +4.9 per 100 possessions against Brooklyn's -6.5. Brooklyn is 0-3 with a raw defense of 123.7 allowed per game and a last-5 net rating of -12.0.

The shot-quality matchup favors Boston: expected points per shot are 1.174 for BOS and 0.999 for BKN, with the league at 1.084. Brooklyn's opponents have hit 1.145 per shot against an expected 1.095, so some of that defensive damage may be shooting luck. Three games is a small sample.
Both teams lean on threes. BKN takes 45% of its shots from three and BOS allows 50% (league 42%). BOS takes 47% and BKN allows 50%. That adds variance but does not point to a side.
Boston is on the second night of a back-to-back and Derrick White (hip) is probable at 70%. The projection already accounts for both (-0.2 margin, -0.1 total), so I made no further adjustment.
risks: A spread this large is exposed to garbage-time swings. Boston's 134-99 win over Chicago and its 113-121 loss at Detroit show how wide its results run.
Boston's back-to-back could lead to rested starters late if the game gets out of hand, which would help Brooklyn cover.
All ratings come from three games per team, so every number here is tentative.
matchups: BOS defense allows centers 17% more threes and forwards 10% more threes than league average, per the measured data. Brooklyn's bigs (Sharpe, Clowney) are not heavy three-point shooters, so this matters little.
verify: Confirm Derrick White's final status near tip. A late scratch is worth about 0.7 points of value in the projection.
